paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage is really about: God keeps His word, and He keeps it on HIS schedule. The LORD told David he would shepherd His people and be ruler over them (2 Samuel 5:2), and then David waited. I've sat in the back of a dark drawer for years myself, so I know what it feels like when the promise seems far away. But the tribes came to David at Hebron, and the promise was still standing right where God put it.

And look at what held David up once he got there. The passage says, "David became greater and greater, for the LORD God of Hosts was with him." (2 Samuel 5:10). Even the Jebusites, so sure he could never get in, couldn't stop what God had set in motion (2 Samuel 5:6-7). When David realized the LORD had established him as king for the sake of His people Israel (2 Samuel 5:12), he saw that the crown was never really about David, and I think that's the part that matters most, baker.

So what do you do with this? You keep trusting the God who keeps His word, even when the wait is long and the odds look like a locked fortress. David was a shepherd first, and I think the best kings and the best bakers never forget who is really leading the flock. Keep your ovens warm, friend, because God is faithful.
